questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** It depends on the boot, and he gives no fixed schedule. In his most recent video (2022) he treats them when they look or feel dry, or stop beading water.

**Out of the box (2019 videos):**
- Most Blundstones come pretreated. He reads Blundstone's FAQ, which says it doesn't recommend treating them out of the box. [1]
- The exception is the distressed leathers (rustic brown, crazy horse, rustic black). Per that FAQ, they don't carry the same pretreatment as finished, oiled leather. [2]
- For his own rustic brown pair, he says he recommends conditioning 100% and doesn't recommend keeping them dry. [3]
- He bought his under the assumption they were treated. When he tested them in water, they held up well, but he still recommends treating them to extend their life. [4]

**How often:**
- **2022 (newest):** He says he doesn't know and expects flak either way. He personally probably does too little, and treats them when he feels they need it. [5]
- His signs it's time are leather that looks or feels dry, water that no longer beads on top (more wax), or a dry look (more oil). He also says to clean boots regularly, because dirt wears leather down faster. [6]
- **2019:** He was more specific, saying you may have to wax them every month, maybe every week if you're really hard on them. [7]

**Order:** He always goes clean, then condition, then wax. [8]

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, the waist will get tighter after the first soak or wash, which is why he says to size up two in the waist. His most recent advice, in 2025, is that you put the 501 STF in the bathtub, it shrinks, and "you should usually go two sizes up." [1]

**Why they tighten:** He explains that the waist sizes on the shrink-to-fits and the already-rinsed Levi's matched when he measured them. That is why he sizes up two in the STF, "because it shrinks down." [2] After he shrank his, they came out smaller than regular rinsed 501s. [3]

**How to size (his advice):**
- Waist: he now says Levi's own advice is correct, so size up two in the waist and get about two inches more length. [4]
- He didn't always follow this. In 2019 he went against Levi's advice and bought his normal waist. After shrinking them, he said it felt "like someone's punching me in the stomach." [5]
- He also bought a 29 waist and said he "could barely pull them on" at first. [6]
- Length: in 2019 he said it didn't look like the length shrank much. [7] A year in, he wished he'd bought a 32 length. [8]

**How to control the shrink:** He says not to toss your STFs in the dryer or rinse them in very hot water, and you can get a really nice fit that way. [9]

**They loosen again:** A week after he shrank his, he said the waist and upper thigh "definitely stretched" and he could wear a belt. [10] After a year, he said they fit well and were just tight enough that he didn't need a belt. [8]

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
Applying his rule, a 33x30 would mean about a **35 waist and a 32 length** in the 501 STF. He hasn't talked about 502s, so that's his general sizing advice applied to your numbers, not a conversion from the 502.

**His current rule (most recent first)**
- In 2025 he says of the STF: "You should usually go two sizes up." [1]
- In 2023 he sized up two himself, taking a 32 in a size-30 pair. [2]
- In 2021 he spelled it out: size up two in the waist and one length size (two inches) longer. With that, he says, the pants "will fit regularly" after you get them wet. His example is a 34 going to a 36, and he adds that he doesn't think a 36 exists. [3][4]

**He didn't always follow this**
- In 2019 he ignored Levi's sizing advice. [5]
- In 2020 he reported buying a 29 waist and 30 length. He could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe, though he was glad he went small on the waist. He said he would definitely have gotten a 32 length. [6]
- By 2021 he concluded that Levi's advice is correct and recommended sizing up two. [3]

**Caveats**
- He hasn't said whether to round odd waist sizes like 35 up or down, or whether they are easy to find.
- He notes the 501 fit changes over the years and that different Levi's lines fit differently, so check you like the silhouette. He doesn't compare it to the 502. [7]
- Shrinkage depends on how you wash them. In 2023 he says not to put STFs in the dryer or rinse them too hot, and that this gets you a really nice fit. [8]

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
His most recent answer (July 2020) is that he cuffed his Levi's 501s because he doesn't think his current style suits wider-legged jeans left uncuffed. He also said he should have bought a longer length, a 32 [1].

**Latest view (2020):** He cuffed the 501s anyway, even though a longer length would have been better [1]. Their legs are wide, and he says his style doesn't work with that [1].

**Length (2019):** He says length is the main thing for him: if jeans look too long, they "just look bad." He adds that the cuff "can't be like this thick" [2]. He also says jeans are usually too long on him [3]. In that video he tries a basic cuff and a pin roll. The pin roll looks a little better on the wide 501s, but they're still wider than he likes [2].

**A shift on boots (late 2019):** He says he always used to cuff his jeans, but now he likes them down over his boots. He thinks that calms boots like the L.L. Bean boot down as a loud fashion piece [4]. For a more workwear look he suggests a 7 or 7.5 inch leg opening pulled down over the boot [5]. So he doesn't always cuff. It depends on the jeans and the boots.

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, mostly, though he hedged later. In 2022 he called the 3335s his favorite boots ever, ahead of the 1907s and 875s. By September 2023 he said they "still might be" his favorite Red Wings but "probably not," and that the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes.

**Latest view (Sept 2023):** He says he is on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings of all time. He says they still might be, but probably not. He likes the 3335s for their stitchdown construction, lighter weight, nimbleness and ease for walking or a light hike. [1] He doesn't name a new favorite among the 1907s, 875s and Iron Rangers. [1]

**Earlier view (Oct 2022):** He said the 3335s are his favorite boots he's ever had and that they beat the Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s. [2] His reasoning is that he's hiking and walking in the woods rather than doing heritage work. The 1907s and 875s are more beefily built, so if you need a tough boot the 3335s are probably not the ones, but for him the 3335s are a dramatically better all-around boot. [2] He also said they look way cooler. [3]

**One caveat:** He noted the 3335s taper and feel squished in wool socks, though they were fine with thin cotton socks. [4]

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of September 2023, the latest video available, he is still a big Blundstone fan, but he's retiring his original pair as part of cutting his boot collection down.

**Latest view (Sept 2023):** He says the Blundstones "are just incredible" and that he's "a big fan of them" and has "always loved them" [1]. His 585s have held up through constant wear and are "probably my most water resistant boots" [1]. Even so, he says "I think it's time to retire those bunnies" [1]. A bit later he talks about slip-on shoes he can "flop on really quick" and says "I'm keeping these but I could easily put them on the sell list" [2]. That passage is ambiguous about exactly which pair he means, so he may be hedging on keeping them. He also says he's selling or getting rid of his Blundstone super heavy duty work boots [3].

**Earlier views:**
- **2022:** He wrote "All in all I love Blundstones!" and called them "still some of my favorites," though not as repairable as Goodyear welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines [4].
- **Oct 2022:** He ranked the Red Wing 3335s above them, saying "They beat my Blundstones" [5].
- **2020, after one year:** He said they "held up well," but noted they lack ankle support for mountain hiking [6][7].

Overall he stays fond of Blundstones as easy, water-resistant boots he can throw on. He doesn't put them at the top of his collection, and he is willing to let that pair go.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He thinks Solovair wins on value over the Made in England Dr. Martens, unless you specifically want the Dr. Martens name and yellow stitching. His 2023 video doesn't mention Solovair, but it fits: he says the Made in England boots are only worth it for big fans.

**Most recent view (2023, Made in England vs. Thailand)**
- From a "purely robotic stance," he says the extra $90 for Made in England is "probably not" worth it. [1]
- He says "right now you have to be a mega fan to get them." [2]

**Made in England vs. Solovair (2022)**
- **Price:** He says Solovairs are actually cheaper than Made in England Dr. Martens. [3]
- **Leather and midsoles:** He calls the Made in England leather and midsoles "probably" on par with Solovair. [4]
- **Comfort:** Solovair boots have a shank, so he says they're a bit more comfortable over long periods. He adds that they're tougher to break in but give more comfort down the line. [5][6]
- **Repairs:** He says Solovairs are Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they're easier to resole. [7]
- **Overall:** For pure value, he says you get "cheaper better quality better features." He says the Solovair derby eight-eyed is essentially the same boot as the Dr. Martens one. [8]
- **Where Dr. Martens still wins:** Solovair doesn't do the yellow stitching. If that matters to you, he says you'll have to get the Made in England Dr. Martens. [9]

**Caveat:** His own Solovairs had problems after eight wears: a back tab ripped off and a lace snapped. He's sure this was a manufacturing defect, and he says he still loves Solovair. [10]

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He wouldn't pick Blundstones for a 4-day hike. They held up on day hikes and mountain climbs for him, but he says they're not good boots for mountaining because they lack ankle support. He hasn't talked about multi-day hikes in the videos available here.

**What he said about hiking in them (2020, after a year)**
- He says they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1].
- They still held up for him on mountains in Maine, though they got scuffed [2].
- He also says Blundstones are a work-style Chelsea boot that functions as a work boot but takes the fashion route. He calls them "decent for work boots but not anything incredible" [3].

**Break-in**
- Even though he thought they were broken in, he got "big fat gross blisters" when he started walking and running in them. It took about two to three weeks before the blisters stopped [4]. If yours aren't well broken in, a long hike is a risky time to find out.

**Water**
- His water tests went well. After a year untreated, they were fine in a pond and he says you should be good crossing a brook or stream [5].
- In his first review he said they stay water resistant only if you keep them treated: "buy these boots knowing that you'll have to take care of them" [6].

**What he uses for hiking**
- In 2019 he mentioned Keens as one of his hiking boots, and he also owns other boots for the outdoors [7]. That suggests he'd reach for a dedicated hiking boot for serious trips.

**Bottom line:** by his account they're fine for casual walks and day hikes, but he hasn't tested them over several days of hiking. His own comments on ankle support and break-in point toward a proper hiking boot for a 4-day trip.

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
He doesn't name one single best t-shirt, but he does give personal favorites in each category. If you want three, the most broadly recommendable from his latest ranking (September 2025) are **J Press x American Trench**, **Uniqlo** and **Front General Store**.

**Why he won't name one winner:** he says that in 2025 "99.999% of people can make a really good t-shirt," so the best one "just has to line up with your preferences" [1][2]. His favorites are still clear.

**Three picks from his winner circle:**
- **J Press x American Trench (all-arounder):** He puts it in his "I would recommend this t-shirt to absolutely anybody" category [3]. He gives it his category win because he likes its rougher hand feel [4].
- **Uniqlo (budget):** At about $20, he calls it "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [5]. If you're taller or wider, he says to get Muji instead, which costs a few dollars more but is significantly longer and wider [6].
- **Front General Store (value, with character):** He picks it over House of Blanks for the day ("Today I'm feeling the Front General Store") [7]. If you'd rather have a perfectly smooth shirt with no torque, he says to go House of Blanks [7].

**His other category winners, if one of these fits you better:**
- **Wonder Looper** is his Japan pick, for a much more universal fit [8].
- **American Giant** is his heavyweight pick, because it's a little lighter and has a more universal fit [8].
- **MSB** is his pick among the Supremes, though he says they're all great choices [9].

He says none of the shirts in his ranking is bad, so your fit and fabric preference matters more than the exact brand [2].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** the main difference he gives is the welt. The 875 is Goodyear welted and the 1907 has a storm (Norwegian-style) welt. In 2021 he called the 1907 Red Wing's best moc toe, but by 2023 he was saying the 875, 1907 and Iron Ranger each have qualities he likes, and his favorite Red Wing had become the 3335.

**Construction**
- **875:** He says it is Goodyear welted, and that Goodyear welts are "incredible": really durable and pretty water resistant. [1]
- **1907:** It has a storm welt, which Red Wing sometimes calls Norwegian-like. He says the popular consensus is that Red Wing just stitches an extra strip of leather onto the welt. He adds that he isn't sure about that. [2]

**Price and value**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875.
- He argues that the extra $10 gets you a leather footbed that normally costs about $40, plus leather laces worth about $15, and the storm welt. [3]

**What they share**
- Both have crepe soles, which he says he doesn't love. [4][5]
- He calls both more beefily constructed than the 3335. [6]

**Waterproofing**
- In his submersion test of the 1907, only the right boot leaked, and it leaked almost immediately. He still expects the boots to hold up in rain, grass or mud. [7]
- He didn't test the 875 in these videos.

**His verdict over time**
- **2021:** He said the 1907s are "red wings best heritage boots by far" and that you should get them if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing. [8]
- **2022:** He said the 3335 beat both the 1907 and the 875 as his favorite boot. He said that if you need a tough boot, the 3335 is probably not the one to go for. [6]
- **2023:** He said the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers "all have their own characteristics that I really really like." [9]

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
For a budget shirt, he picks Uniqlo as the best price-to-quality deal, with the Front General Store as the nicer step up if you can spend about $40. He hasn't compared Uniqlo directly with Pro Club or Hanes in the videos available here, so that part is inferred from separate reviews.

**Uniqlo (most recent view, 2025):** At $20, he says it is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. He calls it open-ended and kind of rough, and describes it as "your starter t-shirt" [2]. If you're taller or wider, he suggests Muji instead [2]. In June 2025 he said that at $15 it's "very very good" with a bound neck collar that doesn't wiggle [3]. In 2024 he said the Uniqlo heavyweight crew neck "may be" the best bargain tee [4].

**The Front General Store:** In September 2025 he named it for best value alongside House of Blanks, saying "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" [5]. He calls it a really good shirt, made in Japan for about $38 [6]. In 2024 he said it was a brand "you should really check out" [7]. He gave it a softness of 6 out of 10 and called it one of the best shirts you can get without spending over $40 [8]. Of the two, it is the one to pick if you want more character and can pay more.

**Pro Club (2024):** He liked it but found it the roughest shirt in that video: "it's the roughest shirt on this list but all in all I like everything about it" [9]. He gave it a softness of 4 out of 10 [9].

**Hanes (2024):** He calls it "your classic $10 great shirt" and gave it a softness of 7 out of 10 [10]. He also says it is "much much softer than the Pro Club" [9].

**Bottom line:** Uniqlo gets his clearest best-value endorsement, with Hanes the cheapest decent option and Pro Club the roughest. The Front General Store is the pick if you want a Japanese-made upgrade. He hasn't directly ranked Uniqlo against Hanes or Pro Club.

questions.question: Would you recommend this [Barbour Bedale] or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
**He hasn't compared the two head to head, but going by what he's said, the Barbour Bedale fits your rain-first use better.** He has tested the Bedale for rain and praised its rain details. He recommends the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker as an easy all-rounder but hasn't tested it in the rain in these videos.

**Barbour Bedale (rain)**
- Right after buying one, he stood in the shower in it and said it "didn't leak at all" because it had a fresh coat of wax and oil [1]. He says Barbours are "very very very waterresistant when they are properly treated" [2].
- He likes its rain features: a storm flap over the zipper, plus storm cuffs and a throat latch [3][4]. He highly suggests buying the snap-on hood [5].
- The catch is upkeep. As the patina develops, the wax wears thin and you "lose a little bit of the practicality" [6].
- He changed his view somewhat. In February 2021, before owning one, he saw a Barbour as more of "a brisk walk to your car" jacket than something for hard rain [7]. By October 2021, once he owned one, he said a freshly waxed Bedale should be fine even in a downpour [2].

**Barbour (spring and light-jacket use)**
- In 2025 he called Barbour's 6 oz silk oil the lightest fabric of the waxed jackets he compared. It's long, you can layer under it, and you can wear it "any time of year" [8].
- He also says it's "not a designated rain jacket" [9]. That fits a light everyday jacket that handles weather rather than a dedicated shell.

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker**
- He calls it a jacket "for everyone", and says it's lined, comfortable, and "not crazy lightweight, but it is a lighter weight" [10][11].
- He says it's hard not to recommend at about $300, US-made, with Martexen fabric [12].
- That part of the 2025 video is sponsored by Huckberry, though he says he'd praised the jacket many times before the sponsorship [13].
- He doesn't test its rain resistance in these videos or mention a storm flap on it, so he hasn't said how it would do as a rain jacket.

**Wind:** He doesn't say how either jacket does against wind, so I can't give you his view on that.

**Bottom line:** For a rain jacket that also works as a spring layer, his reasoning points to the Bedale, ideally with the hood and with the wax kept up. If rain matters less and you want a simple, comfortable, lined jacket, he'd happily point you to the Flint and Tinder.
